explanation.text:
A prayer for deliverance from cunning and malicious enemies, with a confident view of their overthrow, which will honor God and give joy to the righteous. (Psa 64:1-10)

preserve . . . fear--as well as the danger producing it.

bsb.title: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.
bsb.text: Hear, O God, my voice of complaint; preserve my life from dread of the enemy.

explanation.text: insurrection--literally, "uproar," noisy assaults, as well as their secret counsels.

bsb.text: Hide me from the scheming of the wicked, from the mob of workers of iniquity,

explanation.text:
Similar figures for slander (Psa 57:4; Psa 59:7).

bend--literally, "tread," or, "prepared." The allusion is to the mode of bending a bow by treading on it; here, and in Psa 58:7, transferred to arrows.

bsb.text: who sharpen their tongues like swords and aim their bitter words like arrows,

explanation.text:
the perfect--one innocent of the charges made (Psa 18:23).

fear not-- (Psa 55:19), not regarding God.

bsb.text: ambushing the innocent in seclusion, shooting suddenly, without fear.

explanation.text: A sentiment here more fully presented, by depicting their deliberate malice.

bsb.text: They hold fast to their evil purpose; they speak of hiding their snares. “Who will see them?” they say.

explanation.text: This is further evinced by their diligent efforts and deeply laid schemes.

bsb.text: They devise injustice and say, “We have perfected a secret plan.” For the inner man and the heart are mysterious.

explanation.text: The contrast is heightened by representing God as using weapons like theirs.

bsb.text: But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded.

explanation.text:
their . . . tongue to fall, etc.--that is, the consequences of their slanders, etc. (compare Psa 10:2; Psa 31:16).

all that see . . . away--Their partners in evil shall be terrified.

bsb.text: They will be made to stumble, their own tongues turned against them. All who see will shake their heads.

explanation.text:
Men, generally, will acknowledge God's work, and the righteous, rejoicing in it, shall be encouraged to trust Him (Psa 58:10).

Next: Psalms Chapter 65

bsb.text: Then all mankind will fear and proclaim the work of God; so they will ponder what He has done.
Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him; let all the upright in heart exult.
